There is no circular-import risk. triggarr/web/validation.py imports only stdlib, and the import inside the function is fine.

urlparse can raise ValueError on malformed IPv6 brackets. Inside a field_validator that ValueError correctly becomes a ValidationError, so it is not a crash on its own (see bugs-001 for how startup handles that ValidationError).

The runtime load_settings calls in routes.py (lines 1199, 1462, 1511, 1535) reload a file just written from already-validated settings, so the new validator should not fail there unless the file is edited externally at the same time.

findings.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly, redacted error naming the instance and field, then sys.exit(1), like _log_corrupt_config_and_exit
findings.problem: The new validator raises ValueError, which Pydantic turns into ValidationError when the config loads. I read `ensure_config` (triggarr/config.py:333-372). It only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, and its docstring says `pydantic.ValidationError` is left to propagate because it is treated as a 'schema bug'. Before this diff, a URL problem in the operator's file could not cause that. Now a common operator input does: a scheme-less `localhost:7878`, an `ftp://` URL, a link-local address, or a malformed URL on any instance, including a disabled one. The daemon dies with an uncaught traceback from `asyncio.run`, and there is no clean log line naming the bad instance. Pydantic's error text also includes the `input_value`, so a URL with userinfo (`http://user:pass@host`) would be printed to stderr without going through the loguru redacting sink. This is a judgment call on the intended UX.
findings.title: A bad instance URL in the TOML now crashes startup with a raw traceback instead of a friendly exit
findings.why_it_matters: An existing deployment whose config was accepted before this change fails to start after the upgrade, with no actionable message, and may print URL credentials to stderr.

findings.fix_hint: decide on one loopback policy and apply it to both the form path and the config path, or keep an unchanged loopback URL on save
findings.problem: The new config-load validator accepts loopback hosts on purpose (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost). The settings POST handler (triggarr/web/routes.py:560-564) resubmits every instance URL through the strict `validate_arr_url`, which rejects loopback IP literals. An operator whose TOML has `http://127.0.0.1:7878` will start fine. Any later Settings save that includes that instance redirects back with a warning and writes nothing. The diff writes down an intended split between the two validators, but the UI path does not follow it. pending: confirm the settings form always posts every instance's url field (it appears to, from the multi-instance form parsing).
findings.title: Loopback URLs pass the config validator but are rejected by the settings form, so any settings save is blocked
findings.why_it_matters: Same-host users can no longer save any settings change from the UI.

findings.fix_hint: strip the trailing '.' from hostname before the BLOCKED_HOSTS check and reject all-digit/hex numeric hostnames
findings.problem: `validate_arr_url_config` (triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171) compares hostnames exactly against BLOCKED_HOSTS and only parses canonical IP literals. Some inputs get through. `http://metadata.google.internal./` and `http://169.254.169.254./` miss the set match and fail ip_address(), so they are accepted. `http://2852039166/` (decimal 169.254.169.254) is also accepted, and libc getaddrinfo may resolve it to the metadata IP. The strict `validate_arr_url` has the same gap, so this is a pre-existing gap in the helper and the diff only adds another caller. pending: confirm httpx/getaddrinfo resolves the trailing-dot and decimal forms to the metadata address in the deployment image.
findings.title: SSRF validator can be bypassed with a trailing-dot hostname or a decimal/integer IP form
findings.why_it_matters: The control is meant to block cloud-metadata SSRF at config load, and these inputs get past it.

findings.fix_hint: in validate_arr_url / validate_arr_url_config, also attempt ipaddress.ip_address(int(hostname)) / socket.inet_aton-style normalization (or resolve+recheck at connect time) before falling back to the 'treat as DNS hostname' branch, so decimal/hex/octal IPv4 literals are matched against the same blocklist
findings.problem: This diff wires `validate_arr_url_config()` into config-load-time validation, whose stated purpose is to 'still block cloud-metadata addresses (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, etc.)'. That helper (triggarr/web/validation.py:111-173, unchanged by this diff) only recognizes an IP literal via `ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)`, which rejects alternate numeric encodings (pure-decimal, hex, octal) with ValueError, so the hostname falls into the 'treat as DNS name, skip all IP checks' branch. Confirmed on this machine that Python's `socket.getaddrinfo('2852039166', 80)` and `socket.getaddrinfo('0xa9fea9fe', 80)` both resolve directly to 169.254.169.254 via libc inet_aton-style parsing -- the exact address BLOCKED_HOSTS is meant to stop. A URL like `http://2852039166/latest/meta-data/` therefore passes `validate_arr_url_config()` at config load but a real HTTP client (httpx, used for the actual *arr requests) would connect straight to the cloud metadata endpoint. The same gap already exists, unchanged, in the sibling `validate_arr_url()` used by the web settings form (triggarr/web/routes.py:562), so this diff only extends an existing, pre-existing-helper bypass to a second input path (TOML config load) rather than introducing new matching logic. pending: confirm whether any deployment path lets an untrusted party write triggarr.toml directly (bypassing the authenticated settings UI) -- that is the scenario where this second input path actually broadens exposure.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator inherits decimal/hex/octal IP-literal bypass
findings.why_it_matters: If an attacker (or a compromised upstream integration) can ever get a URL value into the config -- directly via the TOML file, or indirectly if a future code path writes instance URLs without going through the authenticated settings form -- an encoded loopback/metadata address slips past the validator and the app's outbound HTTP client would still connect to it, enabling SSRF against cloud metadata services.

findings.problem: This is the first place `validate_arr_url_config()` is ever invoked (it was added unused in a prior commit). `Settings(**data)` is called uncaught in `triggarr/config.py:227` (`load_settings`), which is the startup config loader. If an existing triggarr.toml contains a URL this new validator now rejects (e.g. an instance URL that is disabled but points at a link-local/unspecified/metadata address, or a malformed scheme), `InstanceConfig` construction now raises `pydantic.ValidationError` where previously none was raised for the `url` field via this path, and nothing in `load_settings` catches it.
findings.title: New config-load SSRF validator can crash app startup on previously-valid configs
findings.why_it_matters: This is an intended hardening per the docstring (D-01/D-02), not an attacker-triggered vulnerability, but it is a behavior change worth flagging: a previously-running deployment could fail to start after an upgrade if its stored config has a URL the new validator rejects, which is an availability/operational concern rather than a confidentiality/integrity one.

agent_notes: Abstraction check: validate_arr_url_config is a public function (no underscore) in triggarr/web/validation.py. This is not a reach-in to private internals, so no [high] abstraction finding.

Module-level cycle check: no cycle. models.config -> web.validation -> (stdlib only). triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, so importing the subpackage has no side effects. The concern is layering and coupling, not a runtime cycle.

Duplication (not a finding, below the rule of three): validate_arr_url_config in triggarr/web/validation.py (line 111) is a near-copy of validate_arr_url (line 56). The only difference is that the loopback checks are dropped. That makes 2 copies, so it does not qualify. A single implementation with an allow_loopback: bool parameter would remove the drift risk. This was introduced in the prior commit 14eecb5, not in this diff.

Pattern consistency: putting SSRF validation in a pydantic field_validator matches the existing reject_apikey_in_url field_validator on the same field, which runs at construction time. Raising ValueError so pydantic surfaces a ValidationError matches the CLAUDE.md convention ('Pydantic validation before any config write').
Two @field_validator('url') methods now run in definition order: apikey rejection first, then SSRF. The order does not matter for correctness because each raises independently.

Cross-layer behavior note for the impact/bugs agents: routes.py:561 still calls the stricter validate_arr_url on settings POST, and constructing InstanceConfig then also runs the relaxed validator. A loopback URL is therefore rejected by the UI form but accepted from triggarr.toml. That appears deliberate per D-01/D-02, which is referenced in the docstrings, but no intent doc was provided to confirm it.

findings.problem: Before this change, triggarr/models/config.py imported only stdlib, pydantic and pydantic_settings. It sits at the bottom layer: it is imported by __main__, config, db, state, startup, search/engine, search/scheduler, web/middleware and web/routes. This diff adds the first edge from models into triggarr.web (triggarr.web.validation). web/routes.py already imports models.config, so the two packages now depend on each other in both directions (web.routes -> models.config -> web.validation). There is no module-level import cycle today, because web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only ipaddress, re and urllib.parse.
findings.title: Base config model layer now depends on the web layer, creating package-level mutual coupling
findings.why_it_matters: Every consumer of the config model, including the headless scheduler and engine paths and the tests, now depends on the web package. Any future web/__init__.py side effect, or any import that validation.py later gains from routes or security, would turn this into a real circular import at config-load time, which is the very first thing startup does.

findings.fix_hint: After relocating the validator to a neutral module (see arch-001), import it at module top.
findings.problem: The import is deferred into the validator body. That is the usual workaround for a circular import, but none exists here: web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py is stdlib-only. The deferral is therefore unneeded, and it hides the models->web edge from the module header, from ruff's isort grouping and from anyone scanning imports. It also repeats the import-system lookup on every InstanceConfig url validation.
findings.title: Function-local import hides the new cross-layer dependency even though no cycle requires it
findings.why_it_matters: Hidden layer-crossing imports are how accidental cycles creep in unnoticed. The existing function-local imports in search/scheduler.py (lines 532 and 538, both from web.routes) show this is already a pattern for papering over cross-layer reach, and it should not spread down into the models layer.

agent_notes: Public API: InstanceConfig's signature and fields are unchanged. The only change is an added field_validator on 'url', which runs after reject_apikey_in_url (declaration order). Nothing is incompatible for the 26 importers.

Blast radius: InstanceConfig is constructed on every Settings build. That covers startup (triggarr/config.py:227 load_settings), the settings POST (routes.py:598), add_instance (routes.py:793) and any other endpoint that rebuilds Settings from _settings_to_dict. Every one of these now applies the relaxed SSRF check. The web paths already run the stricter validate_arr_url first (routes.py:561), so the new check is redundant there and can never reject something the web check accepted.

Behavioral asymmetry (pre-existing, not introduced): config load now accepts loopback and localhost URLs, but the settings form's strict validate_arr_url (validation.py:88) rejects them. A same-host user who sets http://127.0.0.1:7878 in TOML and then saves any instance from the web UI gets silently redirected with only a log warning (routes.py:563-564). Worth a product decision on whether the web form should also use the relaxed validator.

Startup failure mode: a now-rejected URL raises an uncaught pydantic.ValidationError from ensure_config. That is consistent with how the existing apikey validator fails, but it gives a traceback instead of the friendly exit path used for TOML corruption. The v2.2 migration (config.py:362) runs before validation, so a migrated config is written first and then fails to load. The .toml.bak backup remains.

Import safety: the function-local import of triggarr.web.validation is safe. triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only stdlib, so there is no circular-import risk. After the first call the import is a sys.modules lookup.
Performance: one urlparse plus at most one ip_address parse per instance, at most 15 instances, and only on settings construction. Negligible.
Schema/DB: no changes to the TOML schema, SQLite or state.json.
Verification: ran the full suite, 982 passed.
Verdict: shippable as-is. This is a tightening change, and the remaining items are capped notes (startup UX for legacy configs, pre-existing gaps in the helper's IP normalization).

So an existing triggarr.toml whose URL is now rejected stops the daemon with a traceback, and a Docker restart policy can turn that into a crash loop. Examples of rejected values: a disabled placeholder like 'radarr:7878' with no scheme, or 'http://0.0.0.0:7878' copied from an *arr bind address. 0.0.0.0 reaches loopback on Linux, which the relaxed design otherwise means to allow. These values are outside the documented contract (README.md:151-179 shows only http://host:port), so this is the control working rather than a regression. pending: show a deployment where a contract-supported URL (http/https with a real hostname) is rejected at validation.py:143-166.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator turns previously-loadable TOML URLs into an uncaught startup ValidationError
findings.why_it_matters: Users upgrading with an unusual but previously tolerated URL get a non-starting container instead of a clear message.

findings.fix_hint: Normalize the hostname (strip a trailing dot; try socket.inet_aton for legacy IPv4 forms) before the BLOCKED_HOSTS and ip_address checks, in both validators
findings.problem: validate_arr_url_config passes hostnames like 'http://2852039166/' or 'http://169.254.43518/' because ipaddress.ip_address() raises ValueError on these forms and the code falls into the 'not an IP literal' branch. Some resolvers then map them to 169.254.169.254. A trailing-dot 'metadata.google.internal.' also misses the BLOCKED_HOSTS set lookup. Both gaps are in the unchanged helper, and the strict validate_arr_url used by every web-form caller already has them. The diff only extends the helper to config load and lets no new input through. pending: show that httpx/the OS resolver in the deployed image turns the integer form into 169.254.169.254.
findings.title: Pre-existing helper gap: integer or shorthand IP hostnames bypass metadata blocking
findings.why_it_matters: It would weaken the cloud-metadata block the new config-load check is meant to enforce, but it is not introduced by this diff.

findings.fix_hint: Catch ValidationError in ensure_config and log only field locations and messages (exc.errors(include_input=False))
findings.problem: Pydantic's ValidationError string includes input_value=<url>. At startup this exception is uncaught (config.py:345), so the full URL goes to stderr through the default traceback, not loguru's redacting sink. If the rejected URL carries userinfo credentials (for example 'ftp://user:pass@host'), the credentials are printed. The sibling reject_apikey_in_url validator already has this pattern. pending: confirm a realistic config where a credential-bearing URL fails this validator and stderr is collected by container logging.
findings.title: A rejected URL is echoed in the uncaught startup traceback outside the redacting log sink
findings.why_it_matters: Container logs are often shipped elsewhere. A credential echo breaks the project's 'never log secrets' rule.
